facts.raw_span: A 22-year-old woman presented for evaluation of malaligned teeth
all permanent teeth had erupted except the third molars in both arches and the lower left lateral incisor
mild spacing between the lower left central incisor and the canine
Class II, Division 1 malocclusion with crowding in the maxillary anterior region
no history of prior dental extractions
an unerupted lower left lateral incisor with an associated well-defined radiopaque lesion in the left mandibular anterior region
a thin radiolucent halo, which appeared to obstruct the eruption path of the tooth

The radiopaque lesion associated with the unerupted tooth is consistent with an odontogenic keratocyst.

The patient has crowding in the maxillary anterior region, which is a common finding in tooth crowding.
The patient has an unerupted tooth, which is a clear indication of an eruption disorder.
The patient has a well-defined radiopaque lesion in the left mandibular anterior region.
The patient presented for evaluation of malaligned teeth, which is a common finding in malocclusion.
The radiopaque lesion associated with the unerupted tooth is consistent with a dentigerous cyst.

rationales.F02: The presence of unerupted teeth suggests potential issues with tooth development or eruption.
